items.title: Diwali has multiple regional meanings

options.text: A single event — Rama's return to Ayodhya

Multiple events depending on region: Rama's return to Ayodhya (north India), Krishna's defeat of Narakasura (south India), Lakshmi's emergence (west India); also marks new year for some Hindu, Jain and Sikh communities

items.reveal:
Diwali (Sanskrit dipavali, 'row of lamps') falls in October-November on the new moon of Kartika. The five-day festival includes Dhanteras (wealth), Naraka Chaturdashi (Krishna's victory), Diwali itself (Lakshmi puja, Rama's return), Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj (siblings).

For Jains, it marks Mahavira's attainment of moksha. For Sikhs, it commemorates Guru Hargobind's release from imprisonment in 1619 (Bandi Chhor Divas).

The festival has become a major UK public event — Leicester's Diwali celebrations are the largest outside India.
items.why: Pan-Hindu festivals can have different narratives in different regions. Treating Diwali as a single myth misses how diverse Hindu practice is and how it links to neighbouring traditions (Jain, Sikh) at the same calendrical moment.

items.title: Vedantic Hinduism teaches the unity of atman and Brahman

options.text: Soul and god are entirely separate

'That thou art' (Chandogya Upanishad 6.8.7) — atman (the individual self) is identical with, or in relation to, Brahman (ultimate reality); different Vedanta schools interpret the relationship as non-dual, qualified non-dual, or dualist
Only Brahman is real; atman is illusion with no relation
Brahman is a god subordinate to atman

items.reveal:
The Mahavakyas ('great sayings') include 'tat tvam asi' (Chandogya 6.8.7), 'aham brahmasmi' (Brihadaranyaka 1.4.10), 'ayam atma brahma' (Mandukya 2).

Shankara (8th century CE) developed Advaita Vedanta — non-duality: atman is identical to Brahman; perceived multiplicity is maya (illusion).

Ramanuja (11th-12th century) taught Vishishtadvaita — qualified non-duality: atman is a real attribute of Brahman but distinct. Madhva (13th century) taught Dvaita — full dualism: souls and God are eternally distinct.

All three schools are orthodox Vedantic positions.
items.why: Hindu philosophy of self is sophisticated. Treating Hinduism as 'just polytheism' misses the metaphysical core that has shaped Indian thought for over two millennia.

items.title: Kant gave multiple formulations of the categorical imperative
items.claim: How does Kant's categorical imperative work?

options.text: A single rule: do unto others as you would have them do to you

Multiple formulations including universalisability ('act only according to that maxim by which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law') and humanity-as-end ('act so as to treat humanity, in your own person or another's, always as an end, never as a means only')
An empirical rule derived from observation

items.reveal:
Kant's 'Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals' (1785) sets out the categorical imperative. Standard count: three formulations.

Formula of Universal Law: 'Act only according to that maxim by which you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.'
Formula of Humanity: 'Act so as to treat humanity... always as an end, never as a means only.'
Formula of the Kingdom of Ends: 'Act according to the maxims of a member of a merely possible kingdom of ends.'

Kant's most famous example — lying to the murderer at the door — shows the strict reading: lying is universally impermissible.
items.why: Kantian ethics is sometimes reduced to 'don't lie'. The multiple formulations and the humanity-as-end principle are richer — and more humane — than the slogan suggests.
